there are differences between clinician-reported toxicity and patient-reported toxicity in rectal cancer, and that the quality of patient reported outcomes in rectal cancer is variable.
the quality of toxicity reporting in RCTs is variable and there is a difference in the toxicity data reported by patients and clinicians.
the quality of reporting toxicity in randomized controlled trials is poor and that there is a need to standardize the way in which toxicity is reported.

the quality of toxicity reporting in randomized trials in rectal cancer.
the reporting of adverse events in clinical trials.
improving the quality of reporting of adverse events in clinical trials of rectal cancer, with the ultimate aim of improving the critical appraisal of the evidence base for clinical practice.

the clinician-reported toxicity data were not sufficient and the PROs data were not sufficient.

clinicians and investigators should be more aware of the differences between patient-reported outcomes and clinician-reported outcomes.
